sources.entry: The Enso Method - Agent skills for Claude Code and Codex that record business assumptions with evidence and confidence, and preserve requirements as the source of truth. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: The Enso Method is a free, MIT-licensed set of agent skills for Claude Code and Codex that turns plain-language outcomes into a PRD and technical design, records business assumptions with confidence levels, and builds software in test-verified phases.
summary.what_it_does: The skills guide an AI coding agent through a staged workflow: writing a product requirements document (PRD) and technical design, having agents review and fix those documents, and researching open technical questions against the real code, data and APIs. Open business decisions are written down in an assumptions register with a proposed answer, evidence and a confidence level, so the build can continue while stakeholders confirm or correct them later. Large work is split into session-sized, shippable phases, and each acceptance criterion is meant to be checked by a test that would fail if the behavior were wrong. The repo also includes closing-out skills that audit whether every criterion was built and proven, and a skill that builds a single HTML stakeholder review package. Documents are kept in the repo after the build so later changes start from recorded decisions.
use_cases: write a PRD and technical design before building with an AI agent
record business assumptions for stakeholders to confirm
split a large feature into shippable phases for AI coding sessions
audit whether every acceptance criterion is built and tested
prepare a stakeholder review package for non-technical decision makers
keep requirements as source of truth across agent sessions
how_to_run: npx skills add EnsoDynamics/enso-method -g  (for other agents such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI)
notable: Assumptions register: business questions are answered with a proposed answer, evidence and confidence level so the build continues without waiting for stakeholders
Review-before-build: agents review and fix the PRD and technical design before implementation starts
Session discipline: each phase is sized to one AI session and ends with a prompt for the next fresh session
Delivery audit and test audit skills check that every acceptance criterion is built and proven by tests
Works on existing systems: the PRD covers the change and the technical design describes only the difference
caveats: Pull requests are generally not accepted; issues and forks are welcome
Requires Claude Code or Codex, or another agent supported by the skills CLI, plus engineering standards to be configured before real projects (per the setup guide)
Skills may direct the agent to use external services such as GitHub, and may touch personal data in project records; data handling depends on the agent and services used
keywords: get ai to build software without guessing
keep docs of decisions for future changes
